editorial_note: Editorial note: Candidate profiles are drawn from Pelham Examiner reporting and candidate statements. This site does not endorse any candidate. All facts sourced from pelhamexaminer.com. Register to vote at elections.ny.gov — registration deadline is typically {{fact:voter-registration-deadline}} the election.

voter_info.label: Register by
voter_info.note: In person or online by October 24. By mail, postmarked by October 19 and received by October 24. Deadlines at elections.ny.gov

voter_info.label: Early voting
voter_info.note: Saturday October 24 through Sunday November 1. Hours and sites: Westchester County Board of Elections

voter_info.label: Where to vote
voter_info.note: Polling places move between elections, so check yours rather than trusting last time: voterlookup.elections.ny.gov. Voting by mail? Apply for an absentee or early mail ballot at elections.ny.gov.

races.title: Board of Trustees
races.context: Context: Hanan Eldahry, who has served since 2018, is not seeking reelection. The central issue in this race is fiscal management — the village passed a {{fact:village-budget-fy2627}} budget with a {{fact:village-budget-increase-fy2627}} increase, overriding the state tax cap for the first time. Three seats are up; top three vote-getters win.

races.title: Board of Trustees
races.context: Context: Maurice Owen-Michaane is stepping down after three two-year terms. The 2025 Manor election was historically close — Lapey won the mayoral race by 20 votes, Case won by 2 after a recount. Kurtz returns for a rematch. Top two vote-getters win.

races.title: Town Supervisor & Town Clerk
races.badge: Re-run required by new state law
races.note: A new state law shifts odd-year municipal elections to even years. As a result, Supervisor Mohan and Clerk Miller — both elected in November 2025 — must run again in 2026 to secure full two-year terms.
races.context: Context: Mohan defeated Republican Dan McLaughlin 2,115 to 1,456 in 2025. Miller defeated Borsella 2,108 to 1,457. Both races were decided by similar margins. Town Council seats (Burke, McLoughlin, Jenks, Curtin — 4-year terms) are not up in 2026.

candidates.name: Russell Solomon
candidates.meta: Incumbent · First elected 2020 · Seeking a third term
candidates.summary: Solomon emphasises a collaborative approach: "I've made it a point to sit down directly with neighbors, local groups and business owners, understand what they need from their village government, and follow through." Key achievements: championed the 25 mph speed limit village-wide, supported hiring a Traffic Safety Officer, and worked on sewer infrastructure (over two miles of pipes repaired). Has served as liaison for pedestrian safety, DPW and downtown business.

candidates.name: Krystal Howell
candidates.summary: Finishing her first term as trustee, Howell is seeking re-election citing unfinished work ahead. "I am seeking re-election because there is still important work ahead — strengthening infrastructure, making serious headway on storm resiliency, improving public and pedestrian safety, supporting local businesses, enhancing village-wide communication, and ensuring that every resident feels seen, heard, and valued." During her term she supported hiring a Traffic Safety Officer, advocated at county and state levels, and worked with neighboring municipalities on quality-of-life issues. She leads with three core principles: respect, empathy and action.

candidates.name: Kristen Burke
candidates.meta: Town Council Member · General Counsel, Mercy University
candidates.summary: Currently serving on the Town of Pelham Town Council (four-year term through 2027) — if elected to the Village board, she will step down. An attorney, Burke serves as General Counsel at Mercy University. Her rationale for running: "One of the reasons I am running for Village Trustee is that currently, while there are three attorneys serving on the Town Board, along with a Town attorney, there are none on the Village board." Her campaign priorities: flood mitigation, rising costs, downtown improvement, pedestrian safety, and sustainability. Motto: "Inserviendo Consummere" — consumed in service.

candidates.name: Arthur Long
candidates.summary: An attorney at Latham & Watkins who ran for the board in 2019. He says the village is at a "tipping point" and that the current board's "unanimous actions have dangerously stretched the Village's finances." His focus is debt and fiscal management: the joint Neighborhood Party platform he signed with Speros and Anzilotti calls the village's path "unsustainable," citing debt growth from $4.3M in 2021 to almost $18M now and a $3.655M Municipal Center authorization that included $800K for furniture. The three pledge to serve without pay, vote against exceeding the tax cap, produce an infrastructure plan, and open up the Picture House RFQ.

candidates.name: Rhett Speros
candidates.summary: A Pelham resident since 2007 with two children in the district's high schools. He runs on affordability — "Our village should be a place where residents can afford to stay" — and on budget management after successive increases in property taxes. With Long and Anzilotti he signed the joint Neighborhood Party platform, which describes the village's current path as "unsustainable" and commits the three to serving without pay, voting against exceeding the tax cap, creating an infrastructure plan, and bringing transparency to the Picture House RFQ.

candidates.name: Paul Anzilotti
candidates.summary: A Pelham resident for more than 50 years, the last 12 of them in the Village. He says he has "18 million reasons" for running — one for each dollar of outstanding village debt — and warns the deficit is "on a trajectory that is unsustainable without continuous substantial tax increases." With Long and Speros he signed the Neighborhood Party's joint platform, which faults undisciplined spending including the $3.655M Municipal Center authorization, and pledges trustees who serve without pay, hold to the tax cap, plan for infrastructure, and open up Village decisions.

candidates.name: Breda Bennett
candidates.summary: Current Deputy Mayor and Police Commissioner. A veteran of the Manor board, Bennett has served since 2018. Running with Liberatore on the Neighborhood Party line, also filed on the Republican line.

candidates.name: Joe Liberatore
candidates.summary: Member of the Village of Pelham Manor Zoning Board of Appeals. First run for elective office. Running alongside Bennett on the Neighborhood Party and Republican lines.

candidates.name: Ryan Kurtz
candidates.summary: Lost to incumbent Tim Case by just 2 votes after a manual recount in the November 2025 election — one of the closest races in Manor history. Running again in 2026 alongside Dlutkowski.

candidates.name: Chris Dlutkowski
candidates.summary: Running alongside Kurtz on the Democratic line. Announced his candidacy in June 2026.

candidates.name: Theresa Mohan
candidates.meta: Incumbent Town Supervisor · First woman elected to the role · Attorney
candidates.summary: Elected Town Supervisor in November 2025, making her the first woman to hold the position. Attorney by training; served as General Counsel and Head of Human Resources for organizations of over 15,000 people; currently teaches leadership and ethics at Fordham Law School. Former Village of Pelham trustee (third term). Campaign theme: "Pelham deserves leaders who won't just maintain what we have, but who will plan boldly for what comes next." During her village tenure, helped secure multiple grants expanding sustainability goals without raising taxes. Running for re-election after less than a year in office due to a New York State law change that requires her to return to the ballot. During her first nine months she has focused on financial systems modernization, facilities planning, and improving resident access to Town government.

candidates.name: Eileen Miller
candidates.summary: Elected Town Clerk in November 2025. Campaign theme: "My experiences will strengthen and enhance communication with town officials." Running for re-election after less than a year in office because of the New York State law change that moves odd-year municipal elections to even years.

candidates.name: Scott Wolfgang
candidates.meta: Challenger · Running for Supervisor · Neighborhood Party
candidates.summary: Launched his joint campaign with Borsella in August 2026 on a platform of fiscal restraint: "We have significant tax and debt growth across most of our other local municipalities and it's imperative that the Town not become yet another financial burden to our taxpayers." Their joint statement: "Pelham's future deserves thoughtful planning. Growth should be balanced with preserving the character, walkability, and small-town charm that make our community so special. Progress should always reflect the voices and values of the people who call Pelham home."

candidates.name: Maureen Borsella
candidates.summary: Lost the 2025 Town Clerk race to Miller 2,108 to 1,457. Running again in 2026. Campaign theme: "The town clerk's position is not just administrative. It is relational. It's about being a trusted, familiar face who helps neighbors."
